subject: Architecture
title: Cahokia: North America's Lost Metropolis
description: A short lesson to help you apply Cahokia: North America's Lost Metropolis.

hook.text: In 1100 AD, a city near modern St. Louis had more people than London at the same time.

buildup.text: Cahokia's Mississippian builders constructed 120 earthen mounds across six square miles.

discovery.text: Monks Mound is 100 feet tall and covers 14 acres — the largest earthwork in the Americas.

twist.text: The city had a wooden sun calendar — posts aligned to mark solstices and equinoxes with precision.

climax.text: Cahokia collapsed by 1400 AD. Deforestation, flooding, and political conflict likely contributed.

punchline.text: Medieval America's greatest city is now a state park most people drive past.

quiz.question: How does Monks Mound compare to other American earthworks?
options: It's the tallest but not the widest
It's the largest earthwork in the Americas
It's smaller than most Maya platforms
